kpis.signal_en: Positive organic growth after two negative years.
kpis.description_en: Comparable sales rose 0.3% in 2025, vs -1.8% in 2024, marking a rebound after a period of slowdown in the housing market.
kpis.explanation_en: Growth in sales at stores open for more than one year, excluding the effects of openings or closings.

kpis.signal_en: Growth driven by acquisitions and comparable sales.
kpis.description_en: Net sales reached $164.7 billion in 2025, up 3.2%, driven by SRS and GMS (+$6.3 billion) despite an extra-day effect in 2024.
kpis.explanation_en: Total sales of merchandise and services after deductions.

kpis.signal_en: Slight marginal contraction despite sales growth.
kpis.description_en: Operating margin fell to 12.7% in 2025 vs 13.5% in 2024, due to cost inflation and post-acquisition investments.
Inventory turnover declined from 4.7 to 4.4, reflecting higher inventory levels in anticipation of demand or tied to acquisition integrations.
kpis.explanation_en: Number of times inventory is renewed during the year.

kpis.signal_en: Very strong operating cash flow, despite investments.
kpis.description_en: Operating cash flow stood at $16.3 billion, used for dividends, debt repayment and capex.
kpis.explanation_en: Cash generated by the company's core activity.

kpis.signal_en: Moderate growth of the physical network.
kpis.description_en: 10 new stores in the United States and 2 in Mexico brought the total to 2,359 stores in 2025.
kpis.explanation_en: Total number of stores open worldwide.

kpis.signal_en: ROIC declining after the GMS acquisition.
kpis.description_en: ROIC fell to 25.7% in 2025 vs 31.3% in 2024, due to higher debt and a pause in share buybacks.
kpis.explanation_en: Measure of profitability on equity and debt used in the business.

kpis.signal_en: Net income of $14.156 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).
kpis.description_en: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).

kpis.signal_en: Dividend per share of $2.33 in the latest year.
kpis.description_en: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.

kpis.signal_en: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $9.152 billion in the latest year.
kpis.description_en: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.

kpis.signal_en: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 64.7% in the latest year.
kpis.description_en: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.

hero_kpi_rationale_en: Home Depot dominates the home improvement market, where comparable store sales (SSS) is the primary indicator of organic growth and commercial health, directly reflecting customer traffic and residential demand dynamics.

ai_positioning.summary_en: The company did not mention artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar terms in the provided excerpts from its 10-K/20-F report. Therefore, its position on AI cannot be determined from this information.

risks.title: Intense Competition from Retailers and Marketplaces
risks.summary_en: Home Depot operates in a highly fragmented and competitive sector, facing traditional retailers, direct suppliers, and online marketplaces (Amazon, etc.). Market fragmentation and the evolution of distribution channels (reseller marketplaces) create growing pressure on market share and margins.
risks.score_rationale_en: Risk mentioned at the very start of Item 1A ('highly competitive, highly fragmented'). Moderate but repeated language. Stable but structural trend. High weighting: direct competition from retailers and emergence of reseller marketplaces threaten the dominant position.

risks.title: Dependence on the Global Supply Chain
risks.summary_en: Home Depot maintains sourcing offices in China, Vietnam, India, Taiwan and Mexico. Trade tariffs, trade restrictions and geopolitical tensions threaten supply costs and product availability. Supply chain diversification remains a major strategic challenge.
risks.score_rationale_en: Explicitly cited in forward-looking statements (tariffs, trade policy, supply chain diversification). Urgent language ('efforts and ability to continue to diversify'). Trend up: tariffs and trade tensions mentioned as future risks. High weighting for an importing retailer.

risks.title: Risks Related to SRS and GMS Acquisitions
risks.summary_en: The acquisition of SRS (roofing, landscape, pool) and its sub-acquisition of GMS (drywall, ceilings, steel framing) represents a major expansion into specialty Pros. Risks include operational integration, realizing expected synergies, and managing 1,250+ new locations with different commercial models.
risks.score_rationale_en: Major acquisitions (SRS in fiscal 2024, GMS in fiscal 2025) with 1,250+ locations. Forward-looking statements explicitly mention 'ability to recognize the anticipated benefits'. Cautious language on integration. Trend new/up: recent acquisitions. High weighting: strategic transformation of the portfolio.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Customer Data Protection
risks.summary_en: Home Depot operates major e-commerce sites (homedepot.com, hdsupply.com, srsdistribution.com, etc.) and collects sensitive customer data. Cyberattacks, data theft and technology disruptions threaten operational continuity, reputation and regulatory compliance (particularly after past sector incidents).
risks.score_rationale_en: Item 1C dedicated to cybersecurity (page 22). Forward-looking statements explicitly cite 'cybersecurity events' as a disruption risk. Increasingly important language. Trend up: cybersecurity is becoming a regulatory and operational issue. High weighting for an omnichannel retailer with massive data.

risks.title: Labor Availability and Costs
risks.summary_en: Home Depot employs tens of thousands of associates across its 2,359 stores and SRS network. Labor shortages, wage increases, union disputes and high turnover threaten customer service quality and operating margins. The 'Drive our core and culture' strategy depends on talent retention.
risks.score_rationale_en: Forward-looking statements mention 'cost and availability of labor' and 'labor disputes' as risks. Moderate but explicit concern. Trend up: post-COVID labor market tensions. High weighting: 2,359 stores + 1,250 SRS locations = massive workforce.

risks.title: Demand Volatility and Economic Cycles
risks.summary_en: Demand for home improvement products depends heavily on economic cycles, mortgage rates, availability of housing credit and consumer confidence. Economic slowdowns, rate hikes or credit crises reduce renovation spending and impact comparable sales.
risks.score_rationale_en: Forward-looking statements cite 'macroeconomic conditions', 'state of the housing and home improvement markets', 'state of the credit markets'. Repeated, nuanced language. Stable but cyclical trend. High weighting: DIY/DIFM demand sensitive to mortgage rates and household confidence.

risks.title: Regulatory and Environmental Compliance
risks.summary_en: Home Depot operates under federal, state and local regulations (EPA, EH&S) in the US, Canada and Mexico. Regulatory changes (taxes, environment, labor, sustainability) and executive orders create compliance risks, fines and operational adjustments. Sustainability and human capital management expectations are increasing.
risks.score_rationale_en: Forward-looking statements mention 'legal and regulatory changes', 'executive orders', 'changes to tax laws'. Moderate language. Stable but rising trend (ESG, EPA). Moderate-to-high weighting: multi-jurisdiction retailer (US, Canada, Mexico) with EH&S obligations.

risks.title: Supply Chain Disruptions and External Events
risks.summary_en: Home Depot relies on a complex distribution and fulfillment center network. Natural disasters, climate change, geopolitical conflicts, health crises and logistical disruptions threaten supply continuity and on-shelf product availability (critical for the strategy).
risks.score_rationale_en: Forward-looking statements cite 'events that could disrupt our business, supply chain, technology infrastructure' (tariffs, natural disasters, climate change, public health, labor disputes). Moderate concern. Trend up: accumulation of risks (geopolitical, climate). High weighting for a complex logistics network.

tagline: The Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retailer based on net sales for fiscal 2025.
